items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1958-08-24
items.q: Then our clients were Charlie McCurdies.

ctx.x: Well they're sitting in back here.

They're flying. No, he wouldn't leave New Orleans. That's how they got Joe Howard on the boat. But you're talking way before the people left. I'm talking, I'm going when we first started on the boat, see. They had Frank Duesen. Oh, gee. That's how they did. Yeah, we were first on the boat. Frank Duesen. They had a guy called James Alexander, drummer. And Manuel come on there for a while, Manuel Perez. Correct. Then we had Andrew Kimberl for a while, see. On trumpet, yeah. On trumpet, see. Then our clients were…

items.title: George "Pops" Foster Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: And we had, I think Charlie McCurdis was on climate.

ctx.x: Guitar. Well he played piano out there. No, he played guitar because he had two guitars and two, because Steve Lewis was on piano. Steve Lewis. Yeah. Well I quit the job out there because I didn't like the way he was serving the fish and stuff that they supposed to give us. I didn't like the way he was serving. And he was giving us a nice way to go. I quit. So I quit like on a Wednesday night, and the whole band quit that Saturday night. So I'm sitting down home. So Peter Bocars and Captain Johnny come to the…
Well, he must have been a pretty old man by this time. Huh? Charlie McCurdis was pretty old probably by this time.
